headline: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.summary: A wildfire health study reported fewer people in temporary housing but 23% still severely food insecure; the committee deferred the item.
meeting.recap: The committee's only item was the Maui Wildfire Exposure Cohort Study.[[0:05:32]] The study, called Maui West, released a new report on July 27, 2026.[[0:06:08]] The share of adults in temporary housing fell from about four in ten to about three in ten.[[0:10:33]] Employment among returning adults rose from 62% to nearly 81%.[[0:17:02]] Food insecurity dropped from about 49.8% to 44.9%, but about 23% remain severely food insecure.[[0:18:37]] Presenters asked council members to help find community spaces for free health screenings under a new program called Hoʻala.[[0:25:43]] A wildfire survivor testified and asked the County to audit subcontractors.[[0:33:57]] Presenters said the study stopped in June for a couple of months because it had no funding.[[0:42:57]] Presenters said County parks have not let them hold screenings because they collect blood.[[1:26:01]] The committee deferred the item without objection.[[1:59:52]]
meeting.next: Presenters said they had not reviewed the food security plan but are happy to review it and give comments. The study team said it will post its screening schedule on its website. The County is meeting with FEMA on how their caseworkers can meet together with residents at the housing site. Council members are to contact the study team to schedule meetings about sites in their districts.

moments.q: "Recovery is underway, but it remains uneven."
Study video: the road to recovery, three years later
"I don't even think Lahaina's in recovery yet."
"They didn't let us use the Parks because we do collect blood from adults."
